text:
alex: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection switch (prefer small-seq kernels past 512) we saw a cluster of GPU OOMs centered on prompt-cache evictions. Dumping notes.

rachel: when did this land? can you attach the evict sample?

perf-bot: ALERT: 2025-11-02T14:12:03Z - GPU OOM x7 on pool:dedicated-usw; p95 latency spike 3.2x

joel: saw similar on canary yesterday. hypothesis: kernel change increases peak memory during batching when seq distribution spikes -> causes slab fragmentation -> triggers aggressive TTL eviction.

alex: repro steps I ran:
```
# run repro (local)
./run_infer --model redwood-v1 --seq 1024 --batch 8 --kernel-policy adaptive
# then tail evict log
tail -n 200 /var/log/kvcache/evict.log | grep compaction | tail -n 50
```

alex: sample evict log snippet:
```
[2025-11-02T14:11:59Z] evict: triggered compaction batch=34 freed=0kb slabs_checked=12 fragmentation=0.78
[2025-11-02T14:12:01Z] evict: aggressive-ttl applied prefix=chat:123 ttl=30 -> evicted=620 entries
[2025-11-02T14:12:02Z] kernel: switched small-seq->large-seq path; kv_mem_peak=1.3GB -> 3.7GB
[2025-11-02T14:12:03Z] OOM: gpu0 task=runtime/infer
```

karen: interesting — the kernel jump causing 3x mem is the issue. we should consider two mitigations: 1) introduce a transient soft-ttl for prefixes touched during kernel transition; 2) make batcher conservative during kernel path switch (cap batch size for N requests after switch).

rachel: can we get hit-rate before and after? alex do you have samples?

alex: hit-rate samples from the 10min window (before/after switch):
```
before: global_hit=0.62 prefix=chat:* hit=0.71
after:  global_hit=0.48 prefix=chat:* hit=0.45
```

joel: that drop explains extra cold lookups -> kernel path memory surge. Also noticed increased key entropy — probably different key normalization when seq>512.

alex: proposal:
- add 10s soft-ttl cooling window on prefixes that see kernel-path change
- reduce batch size to 50% for 5s after kernel switch
- backoff aggressive-ttl if fragmentation>0.6

karen: agree. Also add a perf regression test: synthetic seq distribution driver that toggles between small/large seq and asserts no OOMs and hit-rate>=0.5.

rachel: I'll pick up the soft-ttl PR; joel can you do batcher change? alex add perf job and logs.

alex: assigned. tagging infra: @sre

sre: acknowledged, will monitor.

karen: action items and owners OK? :thumbsup:

joel: lgtm

rachel: lgtm

alex: thanks — I'll post follow-up with PR links.
